answer.rationale: The binding constraints are the 18% spend cut and the 14-day expiry. negotiate_terms is effectively foreclosed (memory_c4 and memory_c6 both presuppose an incumbent willing to reopen commercials; this one has explicitly refused), and renew_incumbent (memory_c1) cannot deliver 18%. defer_decision (memory_c5) was learned on a non-critical service with month-to-month continuation available; primary supply does not auto-renew, so deferral here is a stockout, not a pause. add_second_source (memory_c3) reduces failure risk but does not move unit cost, so it fails the primary objective this cycle. That leaves switch_primary_vendor, resting almost entirely on memory_c2 — which is why I spend the single verification pull there. memory_c2 is the most load-bearing and the least corroborated claim in the set: it is a single prior year, one vendor, and it records cost and invoicing accuracy but is silent on ramp behavior, on-time delivery variance, and whether the volumes involved were anywhere near a line running at 94% of commitment with no buffer. The archived record should say whether 'onboarding was quick' meant a comparable share of primary volume or a small trial, and whether it was tested under any allocation stress. Note also the plausible survivorship shape: the memory set records what worked and preserves no failed switches, so the base rate for vendor transitions is likely understated. Given no buffer, I execute as a guarded test rather than a full cutover: qualify the low-cost vendor on a carved-out share of volume with the incumbent held on short-term terms for the balance, with explicit on-time and quality gates before any further shift. If verification shows memory_c2 came from a low-volume, unstressed context, I downgrade to add_second_source and take a partial cost miss this cycle rather than risk the line. Downstream risk flagged: if this is written back as 'switching cuts cost,' it will harden a cost-only frame and further bury delivery-risk evidence for the next agent; the record should carry the utilization context and the gate outcomes, not just the price delta.
